study.title: Psalm 5 - Prayer of the morning, holiness of God, and protection of the righteous
study.overview: This psalm presents David's prayer as he begins the day. He approaches God with confidence, but also with reverent fear, asking the Lord to hear his voice, judge wickedness and lead him in righteousness. The text strongly contrasts the character of God with that of the ungodly: God is not pleased in wickedness, does not live with the wicked and rejects lies and violence. At the same time, psalm claims that the righteous can enter into the presence of God because of his goodness, and that those who trust in him end surrounded by his protection and favor.

outline.title: The prayer that begins the day
outline.explanation: David asks the Lord to listen to his words and pay attention to his cry. Prayer is deliberate and persevering: he prays in the morning and waits for God's response with hope, not with demand. The psalm begins as a confident conversation with God, the King and the God of David.

outline.title: The holiness of God and the exclusion of wickedness
outline.explanation: The psalmist claims that God has no pleasure in wickedness and that the wicked, the arrogant, the liars and the violent do not remain before him. Here, divine holiness is not only an abstract idea; it manifests itself in real rejection of sin and in judgment against the persistent practice of injustice.

outline.title: Right way, denunciation of the wicked and security of those who trust
outline.explanation: David contrasts his own posture with that of enemies: he enters into the house of God by the greatness of divine goodness, asks for direction in justice and exposes the falsehood of the adversaries. Then he asks God to judge the rebels and concludes with a promise of joy, protection and blessing for all who trust in the Lord and love his name.

study.context: The psalm brings a musical indication in the header and is attributed to David. By the notes provided, this is a morning prayer, with language of trust, expectation and dependence on God. Notes also suggest that the use of blowing instruments in the title is an interpretive possibility, not an absolute certainty.
study.theology: This psalm teaches that God is personally accessible to prayer, but is not morally indifferent. He hears the righteous, but opposes evil, lies and violence. The holiness of God protects the moral meaning of the universe: sin is not only human weakness, but rebellion against the Lord Himself. At the same time, access to God is not born from the merit of the psalmist, but of his goodness. Therefore, the trust of the righteous is not presumption; it is refuge. The text also presents godly life as a guided life: the believer asks for direction to walk on the way of God, and his ultimate hope is to be surrounded by divine favor as by a shield.

scholarViews.insight: The morning prayer expresses firm confidence in God's help; the psalmist begins and ends the day in prayer and awaits the faithfulness and goodness of the Lord without requiring grace, but waiting for it with hope.
David is presented as one who undertakes to continue close to God and his worship, because divine holiness and justice do not turn away the rectum from the heart, but lead him to cling to the Lord.
The joy and security of those who trust the Lord culminate in the image of continuous protection: God's favor functions as a shield that preserves the righteous in every circumstance.

questions: How does my daily prayer reveal real dependence on God, and not just religious habit?
In which areas do I treat sin lightly, when this psalm shows that God opposes wickedness, lies and violence?
Am I seeking only deliverance, or direction to walk in the righteousness of God?
study.practice: Start the day with a short and specific prayer, as in the psalm: ask God to listen, examine your thoughts and lead your steps. Then make an honest self-assessment before God: identify words, intentions, and attitudes that do not match your holiness. Finally, practice concrete trust: give God a situation of opposition or injustice and commit to answer without lies, without revenge and integrity.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided present as conjecture the meaning of the musical title and the association with blowing instruments; therefore, this point was treated with caution. It is also not possible to safely state additional historical details beyond what the header itself and the notes support.
